answer: A newcomer moors at one public jetty and earns standing the slow way: a violet tide-mark beside its berth rises only when strangers confirm real deliveries, and drops sharply on any dispute. The mooring is a ferrous chain — a non-transferable bond of verified compute already spent on public goods, which cannot be lent, pooled, or moved to another identity. A farm's chains all trace back to the same few suppliers, so identical moorings cluster and sink together, and any identity caught faking loses its chain. Privileges grow only as the tide-mark climbs, so headcount alone buys nothing.
